reason: The Azure CLI has no az search index command group (az search covers the service, keys, networking and usage only). Create, update or read an index through the data-plane REST API, for example curl -X PUT "$SEARCH/indexes/<name>?api-version=2026-04-01" with a Bearer token from az account get-access-token --resource https://search.azure.com, or through an Azure SDK SearchIndexClient.

The costmanagement CLI extension has no query command (it has export and show-operation-result only). Call the Cost Management Query API with az rest --method post --url "https://management.azure.com/<scope>/providers/Microsoft.CostManagement/query?api-version=2026-06-01" --body <query definition>.

defaultConfiguration is an index property (semantic.defaultConfiguration in the index definition), not a search service property. Set the service's semantic ranker plan with az search service update --semantic-search free|standard, and the default semantic configuration in the index schema.

The langgraph module has no __version__ attribute (langgraph 1.2.12 raises AttributeError). Read the installed version from package metadata: python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('langgraph'))".
Ollama's API reference marks /api/embeddings as superseded by /api/embed. POST {"model": ..., "input": ...} to /api/embed and read embeddings[0].

Qdrant's OpenAPI specification marks POST /collections/{name}/points/search deprecated from 1.13.3 and drops it from 1.19.0. Use POST /collections/{name}/points/query with a {"query": [...], "filter": {...}, "limit": n} body.

vLLM 0.9.2 added vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc and deprecated vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc; 0.11 hides the old name unless --show-hidden-metrics-for-version=0.10 is passed, and 0.12.0 removes it. Grep or alert on vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc.
Ragas 0.4.3 has no ragas/__main__.py, and its ragas command has no evaluate subcommand. Score from Python with the metrics in ragas.metrics.collections.

An unpinned Inspector resolves to whatever npm tags latest; v1 (1.0.2) prints {"tools": ...} where v2 prints {"result": {"tools": ...}}, so a pinned tool-definition hash silently hashes empty input. Pin the version, for example npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.8.0.
